open_questions.question: The primary link (line 126) opens 'How the fee is agreed with Wedded Wonderland', before the section explains how the fee is agreed. Panel readers rated the CTA 'maybe' (funding_parent, planner_couple, sceptic) or 'no' (search_visitor, uhnw) and wanted the fee basis first. Optional: treat the secondary (line 139, straight after the fee-in-writing line) or closing link as the main conversion point in the CMS CTA block. Not blocking; 08-final.md left unchanged.

The uhnw persona would not enquire through a public form off a blog and wants a private or referral route; search_visitor wanted brand proof. Neither is in brand facts, so nothing was added. Re-run cro-specialist if a discreet enquiry route or proof is confirmed.

payload.rationale: Brief journey_stage is 'comparing': the couple wants to know what they would pay a planner for before they enquire, so the invitation is a Wedded Concierge consultation at /wonderland-concierge. The article deliberately gives no figures, so CTA copy gives none either; the one fee claim is that the fee is agreed in writing before any work begins, which is the promise the panel singled out as reassuring. Each subtext carries a different reassurance once so the fee line is not over-repeated: fee in writing (primary), inclusions in writing (secondary), one named Wedded Advisor (closing). The /wonderland-concierge page's no-cost section is deliberately not echoed, as it would contradict a post about what the fee covers. No perks, Privileges, availability, prices or call-first wording. All four tracked links already appear once each with correct UTMs, so no copy change is made. A printable 'questions to ask a honeymoon planner about fees' checklist would be a better-matched magnet; none is known to exist, so it is a backlog suggestion only and not placed.
